This is Surah 77 (al-Mursalat), verses 1–28 (part 1 of 2), from al-Shawkani's Fath al-Qadir.

It is Meccan according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir.
Qatadah said: except for one verse of it, which is His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾. That verse is Medinan. This is also reported from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The Surah al-Mursalat was revealed at Makkah."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud who said: "While we were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave at Mina, the Surah al-Mursalat was revealed, 'urfan (in succession). He was reciting it, and I was receiving it from his mouth, and his mouth was moist with it, when a snake sprang upon us. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Kill it!' We rushed at it, but it escaped. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'It has been protected from your evil, just as you have been protected from its evil.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that Umm al-Fadl heard him reciting: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾, and she said: "O my son, you have reminded me by your recitation of this Surah. It was the last thing I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in the Maghrib (prayer)."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His saying: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾. The majority of the exegetes said: they are the winds. It was also said they are the angels; this is the view of Muqatil, Abu Salih and al-Kalbi. It was also said they are the prophets.

According to the first view, Allah, glorified is He, swore by the winds sent forth by His command, as in His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ [al-Hijr: 22] and His saying: "He sends the winds," and other such verses.

According to the second view, He swore by the angels sent forth with His revelation, command and prohibition.

According to the third view, He swore by His messengers sent to His servants to convey His laws.

The accusative of ('urfan) may be: either as an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), meaning "sent forth for the sake of 'urf," which is the opposite of nukr (denial/disapproval), and from it is the poet's saying:
"Whoever does good, his reward will not be lost; the 'urf does not vanish between Allah and people."
Or it may be a circumstantial accusative (hal) with the meaning of "consecutive," one following another like the mane of a horse (ka-'urf al-faras). The Arabs say: "The people went to so-and-so 'urfan wahidan" when they headed toward him, and "they were against so-and-so like the mane of the hyena" when they gathered against him. Or it may be an infinitive (masdar), as if he said: "and those sent forth sending," i.e., consecutively. Or it may be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., "and those sent forth with 'urf."

The majority read 'urfan with a sukun on the ra'. 'Isa ibn Umar read it with a damma. It was also said that what is meant by "those sent forth" is the clouds, because of the blessing and punishment in them.

﴿Then those that blow violently﴾, which are the winds that blow strongly.

Al-Qurtubi said, without disagreement: one says "'asafa bi-l-shay'" when he destroys and ruins it, and "naqah 'usuf" means a she-camel that carries its rider swiftly, speeding along like the wind. One also says "'asafat al-harb bi-l-qawm" when war carries them off. It was also said they are the angels entrusted with the winds, driving them. It was also said they drive away the soul of the disbeliever. It was also said they are the destroying signs, such as earthquakes and the like.

﴿And those that spread widely﴾: meaning the winds that bring the rain, spreading out the clouds widely. Or the angels entrusted with the clouds, who spread them out, or who spread their wings in the air at the descent with the revelation. Or they are the rains, because they spread vegetation.

Al-Dahhak said: he means what is spread out of books and the deeds of the children of Adam.

Al-Rabi' said: it is the Resurrection for the Last Day, by the spreading of souls. The waw is used here because it begins another oath.

﴿Then those that separate, separating﴾: meaning the angels who bring what distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between the lawful and the unlawful.

Mujahid said: it is the wind that separates the clouds, scattering them. It is reported from him that they are the verses of the Qur'an that distinguish between truth and falsehood. It was also said they are the messengers, who separated what Allah commanded from what He forbade. This is the view of al-Hasan.

﴿Then those that deliver a reminder﴾: they are the angels.

Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus; that is, they deliver the revelation to the prophets. It was also said it is Jibril, and he was named with the plural form out of honor for him. It was also said they are the messengers who deliver to their peoples what Allah revealed to them; this was said by Qutrub.

The majority read ("fa-l-mulqiyati") with a sukun on the lam and a light qaf, as an active participle. Ibn Abbas read it with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the qaf, from talqiyah, which is the conveying of speech to the addressee. The more probable view is that the first three are for the winds, and the fourth and fifth are for the angels. This is the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, al-Qadi and others.

﴿As an excuse or a warning﴾: their accusative is either as a substitution (badal) for dhikran, or as an object. The governing element for both is the nunated verbal noun, as in His saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾ [al-Balad: 14–15]. Or it is an object of purpose: i.e., for excuse and warning. Or it is a circumstantial accusative by the known interpretation: i.e., making excuse or warning.

The majority read the dhal in both with a sukun.

Zayd ibn Thabit and his son Kharijah ibn Zayd, and Talhah, read them with a damma.

Al-Haramayn (Ibn Kathir and Nafi') and Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read them with a sukun in ('udhran) and a damma in (nudhuran).

The majority read ﴿'udhran aw nudhran﴾ with the conjunction "aw" (or).

Ibrahim al-Taymi and Qatadah read it with the conjunction "wa" (and), without an alif. The meaning is that the angels deliver the revelation as an excuse from Allah to His creation and as a warning of His punishment. Thus said al-Farra'. It was also said: an excuse for the righteous and a warning for the falsifiers.

Abu Ali al-Farisi said: it is possible that ('udhur) and (nudhur) with the heavy form are plurals of 'adhir and nadhir, as in His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [al-Najm: 56]. Then it would be accusative as a circumstantial element of the delivering: i.e., they deliver the reminder in the state of excuse and warning. Or they are two objects of (dhikran): i.e., remember excuse or warning.

Al-Mubarrad said: both in the heavy form are plurals, and the singular is 'adhir and nadhir.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the answer to the oath, saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised will surely occur﴾, i.e., what you are promised of the coming of the Hour and the Resurrection is certain to happen.

Then He, glorified is He, explained when that will occur, saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, i.e., their light is erased and their brightness departs. One says "tamasa al-shay'" when it is effaced and its trace disappears.

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾, i.e., it is opened and cleft. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the sky will be opened and will become gates﴾ [al-Naba': 19].

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, i.e., they are uprooted from their places swiftly. One says "nasafta al-shay'" and "ansaftuhu" when you take it swiftly.

Al-Kalbi said: they are leveled with the earth. The Arabs say: "The she-camel nasafat the pasture," when she grazes it. It was also said: they are made like grain which is winnowed with a winnowing shovel. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be crumbled to dust﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 5]. The first view is preferable.

Al-Mubarrad said: nusifat means they are uprooted from their places.

﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾. The hamza in (uqqitat) is a substitution for a damma waw, and every waw that takes a damma where the damma is inherent may be replaced by a hamza. Abu 'Amr, Shaybah and al-A'raj read it with a waw, and the rest read it with a hamza. Al-waqt is the term at which a thing that is deferred to it occurs. The meaning: a time was set for them for the separation and judgment between them and their nations, as in His saying: ﴿On the day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. It was also said this refers to this world: i.e., the messengers were gathered for their appointed time which had been set for sending down punishment upon those who denied them. The first view is preferable. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: i.e., He made the Day of Judgment and the Separation a time for them. It was also said: they were sent at known times according to what Allah knows.

﴿For what day were they deferred?﴾ This interrogative is for magnification and wonder: i.e., for what great day, at which the servants marvel because of its severity and the abundance of its terrors, has a term been set for their gathering? The clause is a quoted saying of an implied verb, which is the answer to (idha), or it is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial element of the pronoun in (uqqitat). Al-Zajjaj said: the purpose of this appointing is to clarify the time at which they will attend to bear witness against their nations.

Then He explained this day, saying: ﴿For the Day of Separation﴾. Qatadah said: on it people will be separated by their deeds, to Paradise and to the Fire.

Then He magnified that day, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Separation is?﴾, i.e., what will inform you of the Day of Separation? He means it is a wondrous, awesome matter whose measure cannot be grasped. "Ma" is the subject and "adraka" its predicate, or the reverse, as Sibawayh preferred.

Then He mentioned the condition of those who denied that day, saying: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe to them on that awesome day. "Waylun" is originally a masdar that takes the place of its verb, and it was changed to the nominative to indicate permanence. "Al-wayl" means destruction, or it is the name of a valley in Hell. He repeated this verse in this Surah because He divided the woe among them according to the measure of their denial, for each denier of a thing has a punishment in addition to his denial of another thing, and some thing denied is greater in sin than denial of another, so he receives from the woe in proportion to that denial.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what He did to the disbelievers of the earlier nations, saying: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ He, glorified is He, informed of the destruction of the disbelievers of the past nations from the time of Adam to Muhammad ﷺ.

Muqatil said: he means by punishment in this world when they denied their messengers.

﴿Then We follow them with the later ones﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah and those who agreed with them when they denied Muhammad ﷺ.

The majority read (nutbi'uhumu) with a damma, as a resumption: i.e., then We follow them.

Abu al-Baqa' said: it is not conjoined, because conjunction would require the meaning: "We destroyed the former ones, then We followed them with the latter ones in destruction." That is not the case, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.

What indicates the damma is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "thumma sanutbi'uhumu." Al-A'raj and al-Abbas from Abu 'Amr read "nutbi'hum" with a jazm, as a conjunction to "nuhlik." Shihab al-Din said: on the basis that the verb is conjoined to the whole clause "Did We not destroy."

﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals﴾: i.e., like that terrible act, We will do with them. He means whoever We destroy later on. The kaf is in the position of an accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., We will do with every polytheist a destruction like that destruction, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe on the day of that destruction to those who denied the Books of Allah and His messengers. It was said the first woe is for the punishment of the Hereafter, and this one is for the punishment of this world.

﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾, i.e., weak and contemptible, which is the sperm drop.

﴿Then We placed it in a secure place﴾, i.e., a safe place, which is the womb.

﴿For a known period﴾, i.e., until a known measure, which is the duration of pregnancy. It was also said: until it is formed.

(Then We determined.) The majority read "faqadarna" with a light dal. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read it with a shadda, from taqdir. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: they are two dialects with the same meaning. One says "qadartu kadha" and "qaddartuhu." ﴿So how excellent are We as determiners!﴾, i.e., how excellent are We as the determiners. It was said the meaning is: We determined it short or long. It was also said the meaning of "qadarna" is "Our dominion."

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾ — for denying Our power over that.

Then He explained to them the wondrousness of His making and the greatness of His power, so that they might take heed, saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾. The meaning of "kifat" in the language is gathering and collecting; one says "kafata al-shay'" when he gathers and collects it, and from this a saddlebag and a pot are called "kafat." The meaning: Have We not made the earth a container for the living upon its back and the dead in its belly, gathering and collecting them?

al-Farra' said: He means it gathers them alive upon its back in their houses and dwellings, and gathers them dead in its belly, i.e., takes them into possession, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿alive and dead﴾. Sibawayh recited:
"Noble when the vipers gather into their holes from the frost."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "kifatan" means receptacles, and from it is the poet's saying:
"You are today alive above the earth, and tomorrow you will be gathered into the kifat."
i.e., into a grave. It was also said the meaning of making it kifat is that what comes out of a human of waste is buried in it.

Al-Akhfash and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "the living and the dead" are two attributes of the earth: i.e., the earth is divided into the living, which is what grows, and the dead, which is what does not grow.

Al-Farra' said: The accusative of ﴿أحياءً وأمواتًا﴾ ("living and dead") is due to the verb "gathering" (kifat) governing it. That is, "Did We not make the earth a gatherer (kifat) of the living and the dead?" If it is read with tanwin, what follows it is put in the accusative. It was also said that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the earth, meaning: from it such-and-such, and from it such-and-such. It was also said that it is a verbal noun (masdar) described by it for emphasis.

Al-Akhfash said: kifatan is the plural of kafitah, and "the earth" is intended as a collective, so it is described with a plural adjective.

Al-Khalil said: At-takaffut (the act of gathering) is turning a thing over, back to belly or belly to back. It is said: "The people withdrew (inkafatat) to their dwellings," meaning they went away.

﴿And We placed in it firm mountains (rawasi shamikhat)﴾, that is, tall mountains. Ar-rawasi are the firmly fixed ones, and ash-shamikhat are the tall ones; every high thing is shamikh. ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water (furat)﴾, that is, sweet water. Al-furat is sweet water from which one drinks and with which one irrigates.

Muqatil said: All of this is more wondrous than the resurrection.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, for the blessings We bestowed upon them, among Our blessings of which this is a part.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, related from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿And those sent forth in succession (al-mursalat 'urfa)﴾ that he said: They are the angels, sent with goodness (al-'urf).

Ibn Jarir related the same from Ibn Mas'ud.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿wa'l-nashirat nashra﴾: the wind.

Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman related that a man came to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: What are "al-'asifat 'asfa"? He said: The winds.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: the angels.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the angels; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels, who separated truth from falsehood; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: with the revelation.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Woe" (wayl) is a valley in Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows, and it was made for the deniers.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿minma'in mahin﴾ that he said: weak.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding kifatan that he said: a shelter (kinnan).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding ﴿rawasi shamikhat﴾ that he said: towering mountains; and regarding His saying "furatan" that he said: sweet.

He means it is a wondrous, awesome matter whose measure cannot be grasped. "Ma" is the subject and "adraka" its predicate, or the reverse, as Sibawayh preferred.

Then He mentioned the condition of those who denied that day, saying: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe to them on that awesome day. "Waylun" is originally a masdar that takes the place of its verb, and it was changed to the nominative to indicate permanence. "Al-wayl" means destruction, or it is the name of a valley in Hell. He repeated this verse in this Surah because He divided the woe among them according to the measure of their denial, for each denier of a thing has a punishment in addition to his denial of another thing, and some thing denied is greater in sin than denial of another, so he receives from the woe in proportion to that denial.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what He did to the disbelievers of the earlier nations, saying: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ He, glorified is He, informed of the destruction of the disbelievers of the past nations from the time of Adam to Muhammad ﷺ.

Muqatil said: he means by punishment in this world when they denied their messengers.

﴿Then We follow them with the later ones﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah and those who agreed with them when they denied Muhammad ﷺ.

The majority read (nutbi'uhumu) with a damma, as a resumption: i.e., then We follow them.

Abu al-Baqa' said: it is not conjoined, because conjunction would require the meaning: "We destroyed the former ones, then We followed them with the latter ones in destruction." That is not the case, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.

What indicates the damma is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "thumma sanutbi'uhumu." Al-A'raj and al-Abbas from Abu 'Amr read "nutbi'hum" with a jazm, as a conjunction to "nuhlik." Shihab al-Din said: on the basis that the verb is conjoined to the whole clause "Did We not destroy."

﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals﴾: i.e., like that terrible act, We will do with them. He means whoever We destroy later on. The kaf is in the position of an accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., We will do with every polytheist a destruction like that destruction, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe on the day of that destruction to those who denied the Books of Allah and His messengers. It was said the first woe is for the punishment of the Hereafter, and this one is for the punishment of this world.

﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾, i.e., weak and contemptible, which is the sperm drop.

﴿Then We placed it in a secure place﴾, i.e., a safe place, which is the womb.

﴿For a known period﴾, i.e., until a known measure, which is the duration of pregnancy. It was also said: until it is formed.

(Then We determined.) The majority read "faqadarna" with a light dal. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read it with a shadda, from taqdir. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: they are two dialects with the same meaning. One says "qadartu kadha" and "qaddartuhu." ﴿So how excellent are We as determiners!﴾, i.e., how excellent are We as the determiners. It was said the meaning is: We determined it short or long. It was also said the meaning of "qadarna" is "Our dominion."

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾ — for denying Our power over that.

Then He explained to them the wondrousness of His making and the greatness of His power, so that they might take heed, saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾. The meaning of "kifat" in the language is gathering and collecting; one says "kafata al-shay'" when he gathers and collects it, and from this a saddlebag and a pot are called "kafat." The meaning: Have We not made the earth a container for the living upon its back and the dead in its belly, gathering and collecting them?

al-Farra' said: He means it gathers them alive upon its back in their houses and dwellings, and gathers them dead in its belly, i.e., takes them into possession, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿alive and dead﴾. Sibawayh recited:
"Noble when the vipers gather into their holes from the frost."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "kifatan" means receptacles, and from it is the poet's saying:
"You are today alive above the earth, and tomorrow you will be gathered into the kifat."
i.e., into a grave. It was also said the meaning of making it kifat is that what comes out of a human of waste is buried in it.

Al-Akhfash and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "the living and the dead" are two attributes of the earth: i.e., the earth is divided into the living, which is what grows, and the dead, which is what does not grow.

Al-Farra' said: The accusative of ﴿أحياءً وأمواتًا﴾ ("living and dead") is due to the verb "gathering" (kifat) governing it. That is, "Did We not make the earth a gatherer (kifat) of the living and the dead?" If it is read with tanwin, what follows it is put in the accusative. It was also said that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the earth, meaning: from it such-and-such, and from it such-and-such. It was also said that it is a verbal noun (masdar) described by it for emphasis.

Al-Akhfash said: kifatan is the plural of kafitah, and "the earth" is intended as a collective, so it is described with a plural adjective.

Al-Khalil said: At-takaffut (the act of gathering) is turning a thing over, back to belly or belly to back. It is said: "The people withdrew (inkafatat) to their dwellings," meaning they went away.

﴿And We placed in it firm mountains (rawasi shamikhat)﴾, that is, tall mountains. Ar-rawasi are the firmly fixed ones, and ash-shamikhat are the tall ones; every high thing is shamikh. ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water (furat)﴾, that is, sweet water. Al-furat is sweet water from which one drinks and with which one irrigates.

Muqatil said: All of this is more wondrous than the resurrection.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, for the blessings We bestowed upon them, among Our blessings of which this is a part.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, related from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿And those sent forth in succession (al-mursalat 'urfa)﴾ that he said: They are the angels, sent with goodness (al-'urf).

Ibn Jarir related the same from Ibn Mas'ud.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿wa'l-nashirat nashra﴾: the wind.

Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman related that a man came to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: What are "al-'asifat 'asfa"? He said: The winds.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: the angels.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the angels; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels, who separated truth from falsehood; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: with the revelation.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Woe" (wayl) is a valley in Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows, and it was made for the deniers.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿minma'in mahin﴾ that he said: weak.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding kifatan that he said: a shelter (kinnan).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding ﴿rawasi shamikhat﴾ that he said: towering mountains; and regarding His saying "furatan" that he said: sweet.

This is Surah 77 (al-Mursalat), verses 1–28 (part 1 of 2), from al-Shawkani's Fath al-Qadir.

It is Meccan according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir.
Qatadah said: except for one verse of it, which is His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾. That verse is Medinan. This is also reported from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The Surah al-Mursalat was revealed at Makkah."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud who said: "While we were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave at Mina, the Surah al-Mursalat was revealed, 'urfan (in succession). He was reciting it, and I was receiving it from his mouth, and his mouth was moist with it, when a snake sprang upon us. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Kill it!' We rushed at it, but it escaped. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'It has been protected from your evil, just as you have been protected from its evil.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that Umm al-Fadl heard him reciting: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾, and she said: "O my son, you have reminded me by your recitation of this Surah. It was the last thing I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in the Maghrib (prayer)."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His saying: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾. The majority of the exegetes said: they are the winds. It was also said they are the angels; this is the view of Muqatil, Abu Salih and al-Kalbi. It was also said they are the prophets.

According to the first view, Allah, glorified is He, swore by the winds sent forth by His command, as in His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ [al-Hijr: 22] and His saying: "He sends the winds," and other such verses.

According to the second view, He swore by the angels sent forth with His revelation, command and prohibition.

According to the third view, He swore by His messengers sent to His servants to convey His laws.

The accusative of ('urfan) may be: either as an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), meaning "sent forth for the sake of 'urf," which is the opposite of nukr (denial/disapproval), and from it is the poet's saying:
"Whoever does good, his reward will not be lost; the 'urf does not vanish between Allah and people."
Or it may be a circumstantial accusative (hal) with the meaning of "consecutive," one following another like the mane of a horse (ka-'urf al-faras). The Arabs say: "The people went to so-and-so 'urfan wahidan" when they headed toward him, and "they were against so-and-so like the mane of the hyena" when they gathered against him. Or it may be an infinitive (masdar), as if he said: "and those sent forth sending," i.e., consecutively. Or it may be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., "and those sent forth with 'urf."

The majority read 'urfan with a sukun on the ra'. 'Isa ibn Umar read it with a damma. It was also said that what is meant by "those sent forth" is the clouds, because of the blessing and punishment in them.

﴿Then those that blow violently﴾, which are the winds that blow strongly.

Al-Qurtubi said, without disagreement: one says "'asafa bi-l-shay'" when he destroys and ruins it, and "naqah 'usuf" means a she-camel that carries its rider swiftly, speeding along like the wind. One also says "'asafat al-harb bi-l-qawm" when war carries them off. It was also said they are the angels entrusted with the winds, driving them. It was also said they drive away the soul of the disbeliever. It was also said they are the destroying signs, such as earthquakes and the like.

﴿And those that spread widely﴾: meaning the winds that bring the rain, spreading out the clouds widely. Or the angels entrusted with the clouds, who spread them out, or who spread their wings in the air at the descent with the revelation. Or they are the rains, because they spread vegetation.

Al-Dahhak said: he means what is spread out of books and the deeds of the children of Adam.

Al-Rabi' said: it is the Resurrection for the Last Day, by the spreading of souls. The waw is used here because it begins another oath.

﴿Then those that separate, separating﴾: meaning the angels who bring what distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between the lawful and the unlawful.

Mujahid said: it is the wind that separates the clouds, scattering them. It is reported from him that they are the verses of the Qur'an that distinguish between truth and falsehood. It was also said they are the messengers, who separated what Allah commanded from what He forbade. This is the view of al-Hasan.

﴿Then those that deliver a reminder﴾: they are the angels.

Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus; that is, they deliver the revelation to the prophets. It was also said it is Jibril, and he was named with the plural form out of honor for him. It was also said they are the messengers who deliver to their peoples what Allah revealed to them; this was said by Qutrub.

The majority read ("fa-l-mulqiyati") with a sukun on the lam and a light qaf, as an active participle. Ibn Abbas read it with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the qaf, from talqiyah, which is the conveying of speech to the addressee. The more probable view is that the first three are for the winds, and the fourth and fifth are for the angels. This is the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, al-Qadi and others.

﴿As an excuse or a warning﴾: their accusative is either as a substitution (badal) for dhikran, or as an object. The governing element for both is the nunated verbal noun, as in His saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾ [al-Balad: 14–15]. Or it is an object of purpose: i.e., for excuse and warning. Or it is a circumstantial accusative by the known interpretation: i.e., making excuse or warning.

The majority read the dhal in both with a sukun.

Zayd ibn Thabit and his son Kharijah ibn Zayd, and Talhah, read them with a damma.

Al-Haramayn (Ibn Kathir and Nafi') and Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read them with a sukun in ('udhran) and a damma in (nudhuran).

The majority read ﴿'udhran aw nudhran﴾ with the conjunction "aw" (or).

Ibrahim al-Taymi and Qatadah read it with the conjunction "wa" (and), without an alif. The meaning is that the angels deliver the revelation as an excuse from Allah to His creation and as a warning of His punishment. Thus said al-Farra'. It was also said: an excuse for the righteous and a warning for the falsifiers.

Abu Ali al-Farisi said: it is possible that ('udhur) and (nudhur) with the heavy form are plurals of 'adhir and nadhir, as in His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [al-Najm: 56]. Then it would be accusative as a circumstantial element of the delivering: i.e., they deliver the reminder in the state of excuse and warning. Or they are two objects of (dhikran): i.e., remember excuse or warning.

Al-Mubarrad said: both in the heavy form are plurals, and the singular is 'adhir and nadhir.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the answer to the oath, saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised will surely occur﴾, i.e., what you are promised of the coming of the Hour and the Resurrection is certain to happen.

Then He, glorified is He, explained when that will occur, saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, i.e., their light is erased and their brightness departs. One says "tamasa al-shay'" when it is effaced and its trace disappears.

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾, i.e., it is opened and cleft. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the sky will be opened and will become gates﴾ [al-Naba': 19].

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, i.e., they are uprooted from their places swiftly. One says "nasafta al-shay'" and "ansaftuhu" when you take it swiftly.

Al-Kalbi said: they are leveled with the earth. The Arabs say: "The she-camel nasafat the pasture," when she grazes it. It was also said: they are made like grain which is winnowed with a winnowing shovel. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be crumbled to dust﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 5]. The first view is preferable.

Al-Mubarrad said: nusifat means they are uprooted from their places.

﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾. The hamza in (uqqitat) is a substitution for a damma waw, and every waw that takes a damma where the damma is inherent may be replaced by a hamza. Abu 'Amr, Shaybah and al-A'raj read it with a waw, and the rest read it with a hamza. Al-waqt is the term at which a thing that is deferred to it occurs. The meaning: a time was set for them for the separation and judgment between them and their nations, as in His saying: ﴿On the day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. It was also said this refers to this world: i.e., the messengers were gathered for their appointed time which had been set for sending down punishment upon those who denied them. The first view is preferable. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: i.e., He made the Day of Judgment and the Separation a time for them. It was also said: they were sent at known times according to what Allah knows.

﴿For what day were they deferred?﴾ This interrogative is for magnification and wonder: i.e., for what great day, at which the servants marvel because of its severity and the abundance of its terrors, has a term been set for their gathering? The clause is a quoted saying of an implied verb, which is the answer to (idha), or it is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial element of the pronoun in (uqqitat). Al-Zajjaj said: the purpose of this appointing is to clarify the time at which they will attend to bear witness against their nations.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that Umm al-Fadl heard him reciting: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾, and she said: "O my son, you have reminded me by your recitation of this Surah. It was the last thing I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in the Maghrib (prayer)."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His saying: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾. The majority of the exegetes said: they are the winds. It was also said they are the angels; this is the view of Muqatil, Abu Salih and al-Kalbi. It was also said they are the prophets.

According to the first view, Allah, glorified is He, swore by the winds sent forth by His command, as in His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ [al-Hijr: 22] and His saying: "He sends the winds," and other such verses.

According to the second view, He swore by the angels sent forth with His revelation, command and prohibition.

According to the third view, He swore by His messengers sent to His servants to convey His laws.

The accusative of ('urfan) may be: either as an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), meaning "sent forth for the sake of 'urf," which is the opposite of nukr (denial/disapproval), and from it is the poet's saying:
"Whoever does good, his reward will not be lost; the 'urf does not vanish between Allah and people."
Or it may be a circumstantial accusative (hal) with the meaning of "consecutive," one following another like the mane of a horse (ka-'urf al-faras). The Arabs say: "The people went to so-and-so 'urfan wahidan" when they headed toward him, and "they were against so-and-so like the mane of the hyena" when they gathered against him. Or it may be an infinitive (masdar), as if he said: "and those sent forth sending," i.e., consecutively. Or it may be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., "and those sent forth with 'urf."

The majority read 'urfan with a sukun on the ra'. 'Isa ibn Umar read it with a damma. It was also said that what is meant by "those sent forth" is the clouds, because of the blessing and punishment in them.

﴿Then those that blow violently﴾, which are the winds that blow strongly.

Al-Qurtubi said, without disagreement: one says "'asafa bi-l-shay'" when he destroys and ruins it, and "naqah 'usuf" means a she-camel that carries its rider swiftly, speeding along like the wind. One also says "'asafat al-harb bi-l-qawm" when war carries them off. It was also said they are the angels entrusted with the winds, driving them. It was also said they drive away the soul of the disbeliever. It was also said they are the destroying signs, such as earthquakes and the like.

﴿And those that spread widely﴾: meaning the winds that bring the rain, spreading out the clouds widely. Or the angels entrusted with the clouds, who spread them out, or who spread their wings in the air at the descent with the revelation. Or they are the rains, because they spread vegetation.

Al-Dahhak said: he means what is spread out of books and the deeds of the children of Adam.

Al-Rabi' said: it is the Resurrection for the Last Day, by the spreading of souls. The waw is used here because it begins another oath.

﴿Then those that separate, separating﴾: meaning the angels who bring what distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between the lawful and the unlawful.

Mujahid said: it is the wind that separates the clouds, scattering them. It is reported from him that they are the verses of the Qur'an that distinguish between truth and falsehood. It was also said they are the messengers, who separated what Allah commanded from what He forbade. This is the view of al-Hasan.

﴿Then those that deliver a reminder﴾: they are the angels.

Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus; that is, they deliver the revelation to the prophets. It was also said it is Jibril, and he was named with the plural form out of honor for him. It was also said they are the messengers who deliver to their peoples what Allah revealed to them; this was said by Qutrub.

The majority read ("fa-l-mulqiyati") with a sukun on the lam and a light qaf, as an active participle. Ibn Abbas read it with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the qaf, from talqiyah, which is the conveying of speech to the addressee. The more probable view is that the first three are for the winds, and the fourth and fifth are for the angels. This is the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, al-Qadi and others.

﴿As an excuse or a warning﴾: their accusative is either as a substitution (badal) for dhikran, or as an object. The governing element for both is the nunated verbal noun, as in His saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾ [al-Balad: 14–15]. Or it is an object of purpose: i.e., for excuse and warning. Or it is a circumstantial accusative by the known interpretation: i.e., making excuse or warning.

The majority read the dhal in both with a sukun.

Zayd ibn Thabit and his son Kharijah ibn Zayd, and Talhah, read them with a damma.

Al-Haramayn (Ibn Kathir and Nafi') and Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read them with a sukun in ('udhran) and a damma in (nudhuran).

The majority read ﴿'udhran aw nudhran﴾ with the conjunction "aw" (or).

Ibrahim al-Taymi and Qatadah read it with the conjunction "wa" (and), without an alif. The meaning is that the angels deliver the revelation as an excuse from Allah to His creation and as a warning of His punishment. Thus said al-Farra'. It was also said: an excuse for the righteous and a warning for the falsifiers.

Abu Ali al-Farisi said: it is possible that ('udhur) and (nudhur) with the heavy form are plurals of 'adhir and nadhir, as in His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [al-Najm: 56]. Then it would be accusative as a circumstantial element of the delivering: i.e., they deliver the reminder in the state of excuse and warning. Or they are two objects of (dhikran): i.e., remember excuse or warning.

Al-Mubarrad said: both in the heavy form are plurals, and the singular is 'adhir and nadhir.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the answer to the oath, saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised will surely occur﴾, i.e., what you are promised of the coming of the Hour and the Resurrection is certain to happen.

Then He, glorified is He, explained when that will occur, saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, i.e., their light is erased and their brightness departs. One says "tamasa al-shay'" when it is effaced and its trace disappears.

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾, i.e., it is opened and cleft. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the sky will be opened and will become gates﴾ [al-Naba': 19].

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, i.e., they are uprooted from their places swiftly. One says "nasafta al-shay'" and "ansaftuhu" when you take it swiftly.

Al-Kalbi said: they are leveled with the earth. The Arabs say: "The she-camel nasafat the pasture," when she grazes it. It was also said: they are made like grain which is winnowed with a winnowing shovel. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be crumbled to dust﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 5]. The first view is preferable.

Al-Mubarrad said: nusifat means they are uprooted from their places.

﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾. The hamza in (uqqitat) is a substitution for a damma waw, and every waw that takes a damma where the damma is inherent may be replaced by a hamza. Abu 'Amr, Shaybah and al-A'raj read it with a waw, and the rest read it with a hamza. Al-waqt is the term at which a thing that is deferred to it occurs. The meaning: a time was set for them for the separation and judgment between them and their nations, as in His saying: ﴿On the day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. It was also said this refers to this world: i.e., the messengers were gathered for their appointed time which had been set for sending down punishment upon those who denied them. The first view is preferable. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: i.e., He made the Day of Judgment and the Separation a time for them. It was also said: they were sent at known times according to what Allah knows.

﴿For what day were they deferred?﴾ This interrogative is for magnification and wonder: i.e., for what great day, at which the servants marvel because of its severity and the abundance of its terrors, has a term been set for their gathering? The clause is a quoted saying of an implied verb, which is the answer to (idha), or it is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial element of the pronoun in (uqqitat). Al-Zajjaj said: the purpose of this appointing is to clarify the time at which they will attend to bear witness against their nations.

Then He explained this day, saying: ﴿For the Day of Separation﴾. Qatadah said: on it people will be separated by their deeds, to Paradise and to the Fire.

Then He magnified that day, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Separation is?﴾, i.e., what will inform you of the Day of Separation? He means it is a wondrous, awesome matter whose measure cannot be grasped. "Ma" is the subject and "adraka" its predicate, or the reverse, as Sibawayh preferred.

Then He mentioned the condition of those who denied that day, saying: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe to them on that awesome day. "Waylun" is originally a masdar that takes the place of its verb, and it was changed to the nominative to indicate permanence. "Al-wayl" means destruction, or it is the name of a valley in Hell. He repeated this verse in this Surah because He divided the woe among them according to the measure of their denial, for each denier of a thing has a punishment in addition to his denial of another thing, and some thing denied is greater in sin than denial of another, so he receives from the woe in proportion to that denial.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what He did to the disbelievers of the earlier nations, saying: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ He, glorified is He, informed of the destruction of the disbelievers of the past nations from the time of Adam to Muhammad ﷺ.

Muqatil said: he means by punishment in this world when they denied their messengers.

﴿Then We follow them with the later ones﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah and those who agreed with them when they denied Muhammad ﷺ.

The majority read (nutbi'uhumu) with a damma, as a resumption: i.e., then We follow them.

Abu al-Baqa' said: it is not conjoined, because conjunction would require the meaning: "We destroyed the former ones, then We followed them with the latter ones in destruction." That is not the case, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.

What indicates the damma is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "thumma sanutbi'uhumu." Al-A'raj and al-Abbas from Abu 'Amr read "nutbi'hum" with a jazm, as a conjunction to "nuhlik." Shihab al-Din said: on the basis that the verb is conjoined to the whole clause "Did We not destroy."

﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals﴾: i.e., like that terrible act, We will do with them. He means whoever We destroy later on. The kaf is in the position of an accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., We will do with every polytheist a destruction like that destruction, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe on the day of that destruction to those who denied the Books of Allah and His messengers. It was said the first woe is for the punishment of the Hereafter, and this one is for the punishment of this world.

﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾, i.e., weak and contemptible, which is the sperm drop.

﴿Then We placed it in a secure place﴾, i.e., a safe place, which is the womb.

﴿For a known period﴾, i.e., until a known measure, which is the duration of pregnancy. It was also said: until it is formed.

(Then We determined.) The majority read "faqadarna" with a light dal. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read it with a shadda, from taqdir. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: they are two dialects with the same meaning. One says "qadartu kadha" and "qaddartuhu." ﴿So how excellent are We as determiners!﴾, i.e., how excellent are We as the determiners. It was said the meaning is: We determined it short or long. It was also said the meaning of "qadarna" is "Our dominion."

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾ — for denying Our power over that.

Then He explained to them the wondrousness of His making and the greatness of His power, so that they might take heed, saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾. The meaning of "kifat" in the language is gathering and collecting; one says "kafata al-shay'" when he gathers and collects it, and from this a saddlebag and a pot are called "kafat." The meaning: Have We not made the earth a container for the living upon its back and the dead in its belly, gathering and collecting them?

al-Farra' said: He means it gathers them alive upon its back in their houses and dwellings, and gathers them dead in its belly, i.e., takes them into possession, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿alive and dead﴾. Sibawayh recited:
"Noble when the vipers gather into their holes from the frost."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "kifatan" means receptacles, and from it is the poet's saying:
"You are today alive above the earth, and tomorrow you will be gathered into the kifat."
i.e., into a grave. It was also said the meaning of making it kifat is that what comes out of a human of waste is buried in it.

Al-Akhfash and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "the living and the dead" are two attributes of the earth: i.e., the earth is divided into the living, which is what grows, and the dead, which is what does not grow.

Al-Farra' said: The accusative of ﴿أحياءً وأمواتًا﴾ ("living and dead") is due to the verb "gathering" (kifat) governing it. That is, "Did We not make the earth a gatherer (kifat) of the living and the dead?" If it is read with tanwin, what follows it is put in the accusative. It was also said that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the earth, meaning: from it such-and-such, and from it such-and-such. It was also said that it is a verbal noun (masdar) described by it for emphasis.

Al-Akhfash said: kifatan is the plural of kafitah, and "the earth" is intended as a collective, so it is described with a plural adjective.

Al-Khalil said: At-takaffut (the act of gathering) is turning a thing over, back to belly or belly to back. It is said: "The people withdrew (inkafatat) to their dwellings," meaning they went away.

﴿And We placed in it firm mountains (rawasi shamikhat)﴾, that is, tall mountains. Ar-rawasi are the firmly fixed ones, and ash-shamikhat are the tall ones; every high thing is shamikh. ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water (furat)﴾, that is, sweet water. Al-furat is sweet water from which one drinks and with which one irrigates.

Muqatil said: All of this is more wondrous than the resurrection.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, for the blessings We bestowed upon them, among Our blessings of which this is a part.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, related from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿And those sent forth in succession (al-mursalat 'urfa)﴾ that he said: They are the angels, sent with goodness (al-'urf).

Ibn Jarir related the same from Ibn Mas'ud.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿wa'l-nashirat nashra﴾: the wind.

Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman related that a man came to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: What are "al-'asifat 'asfa"? He said: The winds.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: the angels.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the angels; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels, who separated truth from falsehood; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: with the revelation.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Woe" (wayl) is a valley in Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows, and it was made for the deniers.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿minma'in mahin﴾ that he said: weak.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding kifatan that he said: a shelter (kinnan).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding ﴿rawasi shamikhat﴾ that he said: towering mountains; and regarding His saying "furatan" that he said: sweet.

This is Surah 77 (al-Mursalat), verses 1–28 (part 1 of 2), from al-Shawkani's Fath al-Qadir.

It is Meccan according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir.
Qatadah said: except for one verse of it, which is His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾. That verse is Medinan. This is also reported from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The Surah al-Mursalat was revealed at Makkah."

He was reciting it, and I was receiving it from his mouth, and his mouth was moist with it, when a snake sprang upon us. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Kill it!' We rushed at it, but it escaped. Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what He did to the disbelievers of the earlier nations, saying: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ He, glorified is He, informed of the destruction of the disbelievers of the past nations from the time of Adam to Muhammad ﷺ.

Muqatil said: he means by punishment in this world when they denied their messengers.

﴿Then We follow them with the later ones﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah and those who agreed with them when they denied Muhammad ﷺ.

The majority read (nutbi'uhumu) with a damma, as a resumption: i.e., then We follow them.

Abu al-Baqa' said: it is not conjoined, because conjunction would require the meaning: "We destroyed the former ones, then We followed them with the latter ones in destruction." That is not the case, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.

What indicates the damma is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "thumma sanutbi'uhumu." Al-A'raj and al-Abbas from Abu 'Amr read "nutbi'hum" with a jazm, as a conjunction to "nuhlik." Shihab al-Din said: on the basis that the verb is conjoined to the whole clause "Did We not destroy."

﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals﴾: i.e., like that terrible act, We will do with them. He means whoever We destroy later on. The kaf is in the position of an accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., We will do with every polytheist a destruction like that destruction, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe on the day of that destruction to those who denied the Books of Allah and His messengers. It was said the first woe is for the punishment of the Hereafter, and this one is for the punishment of this world.

﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾, i.e., weak and contemptible, which is the sperm drop.

﴿Then We placed it in a secure place﴾, i.e., a safe place, which is the womb.

﴿For a known period﴾, i.e., until a known measure, which is the duration of pregnancy. It was also said: until it is formed.

(Then We determined.) The majority read "faqadarna" with a light dal. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read it with a shadda, from taqdir. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: they are two dialects with the same meaning. One says "qadartu kadha" and "qaddartuhu." ﴿So how excellent are We as determiners!﴾, i.e., how excellent are We as the determiners. It was said the meaning is: We determined it short or long. It was also said the meaning of "qadarna" is "Our dominion."

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾ — for denying Our power over that.

Then He explained to them the wondrousness of His making and the greatness of His power, so that they might take heed, saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾. The meaning of "kifat" in the language is gathering and collecting; one says "kafata al-shay'" when he gathers and collects it, and from this a saddlebag and a pot are called "kafat." The meaning: Have We not made the earth a container for the living upon its back and the dead in its belly, gathering and collecting them?

al-Farra' said: He means it gathers them alive upon its back in their houses and dwellings, and gathers them dead in its belly, i.e., takes them into possession, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿alive and dead﴾. Sibawayh recited:
"Noble when the vipers gather into their holes from the frost."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "kifatan" means receptacles, and from it is the poet's saying:
"You are today alive above the earth, and tomorrow you will be gathered into the kifat."
i.e., into a grave. It was also said the meaning of making it kifat is that what comes out of a human of waste is buried in it.

Al-Akhfash and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "the living and the dead" are two attributes of the earth: i.e., the earth is divided into the living, which is what grows, and the dead, which is what does not grow.

Al-Farra' said: The accusative of ﴿أحياءً وأمواتًا﴾ ("living and dead") is due to the verb "gathering" (kifat) governing it. That is, "Did We not make the earth a gatherer (kifat) of the living and the dead?" If it is read with tanwin, what follows it is put in the accusative. It was also said that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the earth, meaning: from it such-and-such, and from it such-and-such. It was also said that it is a verbal noun (masdar) described by it for emphasis.

Al-Akhfash said: kifatan is the plural of kafitah, and "the earth" is intended as a collective, so it is described with a plural adjective.

Al-Khalil said: At-takaffut (the act of gathering) is turning a thing over, back to belly or belly to back. It is said: "The people withdrew (inkafatat) to their dwellings," meaning they went away.

﴿And We placed in it firm mountains (rawasi shamikhat)﴾, that is, tall mountains. Ar-rawasi are the firmly fixed ones, and ash-shamikhat are the tall ones; every high thing is shamikh. ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water (furat)﴾, that is, sweet water. Al-furat is sweet water from which one drinks and with which one irrigates.

Muqatil said: All of this is more wondrous than the resurrection.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, for the blessings We bestowed upon them, among Our blessings of which this is a part.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, related from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿And those sent forth in succession (al-mursalat 'urfa)﴾ that he said: They are the angels, sent with goodness (al-'urf).

Ibn Jarir related the same from Ibn Mas'ud.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿wa'l-nashirat nashra﴾: the wind.

Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman related that a man came to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: What are "al-'asifat 'asfa"? He said: The winds.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the wind; ﴿fa'l-'asifat 'asfa﴾: the wind; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: the angels.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding ﴿al-mursalat 'urfa﴾ that he said: the angels; ﴿fa'l-fariqat farqa﴾: the angels, who separated truth from falsehood; ﴿fa'l-mulqiyat dhikra﴾: with the revelation.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Woe" (wayl) is a valley in Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows, and it was made for the deniers.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿minma'in mahin﴾ that he said: weak.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding kifatan that he said: a shelter (kinnan).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding ﴿rawasi shamikhat﴾ that he said: towering mountains; and regarding His saying "furatan" that he said: sweet.

This is Surah 77 (al-Mursalat), verses 1–28 (part 1 of 2), from al-Shawkani's Fath al-Qadir.

It is Meccan according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir.
Qatadah said: except for one verse of it, which is His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾. That verse is Medinan. This is also reported from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The Surah al-Mursalat was revealed at Makkah."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud who said: "While we were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave at Mina, the Surah al-Mursalat was revealed, 'urfan (in succession). He was reciting it, and I was receiving it from his mouth, and his mouth was moist with it, when a snake sprang upon us. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Kill it!' We rushed at it, but it escaped. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'It has been protected from your evil, just as you have been protected from its evil.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that Umm al-Fadl heard him reciting: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾, and she said: "O my son, you have reminded me by your recitation of this Surah. It was the last thing I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in the Maghrib (prayer)."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His saying: ﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾. The majority of the exegetes said: they are the winds. It was also said they are the angels; this is the view of Muqatil, Abu Salih and al-Kalbi. It was also said they are the prophets.

According to the first view, Allah, glorified is He, swore by the winds sent forth by His command, as in His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ [al-Hijr: 22] and His saying: "He sends the winds," and other such verses.

According to the second view, He swore by the angels sent forth with His revelation, command and prohibition.

According to the third view, He swore by His messengers sent to His servants to convey His laws.

The accusative of ('urfan) may be: either as an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), meaning "sent forth for the sake of 'urf," which is the opposite of nukr (denial/disapproval), and from it is the poet's saying:
"Whoever does good, his reward will not be lost; the 'urf does not vanish between Allah and people."
Or it may be a circumstantial accusative (hal) with the meaning of "consecutive," one following another like the mane of a horse (ka-'urf al-faras). The Arabs say: "The people went to so-and-so 'urfan wahidan" when they headed toward him, and "they were against so-and-so like the mane of the hyena" when they gathered against him. Or it may be an infinitive (masdar), as if he said: "and those sent forth sending," i.e., consecutively. Or it may be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., "and those sent forth with 'urf."

The majority read 'urfan with a sukun on the ra'. 'Isa ibn Umar read it with a damma. It was also said that what is meant by "those sent forth" is the clouds, because of the blessing and punishment in them.

﴿Then those that blow violently﴾, which are the winds that blow strongly.

Al-Qurtubi said, without disagreement: one says "'asafa bi-l-shay'" when he destroys and ruins it, and "naqah 'usuf" means a she-camel that carries its rider swiftly, speeding along like the wind. One also says "'asafat al-harb bi-l-qawm" when war carries them off. It was also said they are the angels entrusted with the winds, driving them. It was also said they drive away the soul of the disbeliever. It was also said they are the destroying signs, such as earthquakes and the like.

﴿And those that spread widely﴾: meaning the winds that bring the rain, spreading out the clouds widely. Or the angels entrusted with the clouds, who spread them out, or who spread their wings in the air at the descent with the revelation. Or they are the rains, because they spread vegetation.

Al-Dahhak said: he means what is spread out of books and the deeds of the children of Adam.

Al-Rabi' said: it is the Resurrection for the Last Day, by the spreading of souls. The waw is used here because it begins another oath.

﴿Then those that separate, separating﴾: meaning the angels who bring what distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between the lawful and the unlawful.

Mujahid said: it is the wind that separates the clouds, scattering them. It is reported from him that they are the verses of the Qur'an that distinguish between truth and falsehood. It was also said they are the messengers, who separated what Allah commanded from what He forbade. This is the view of al-Hasan.

﴿Then those that deliver a reminder﴾: they are the angels.

Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus; that is, they deliver the revelation to the prophets. It was also said it is Jibril, and he was named with the plural form out of honor for him. It was also said they are the messengers who deliver to their peoples what Allah revealed to them; this was said by Qutrub.

The majority read ("fa-l-mulqiyati") with a sukun on the lam and a light qaf, as an active participle. Ibn Abbas read it with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the qaf, from talqiyah, which is the conveying of speech to the addressee. The more probable view is that the first three are for the winds, and the fourth and fifth are for the angels. This is the view chosen by al-Zajjaj, al-Qadi and others.

﴿As an excuse or a warning﴾: their accusative is either as a substitution (badal) for dhikran, or as an object. The governing element for both is the nunated verbal noun, as in His saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾ [al-Balad: 14–15]. Or it is an object of purpose: i.e., for excuse and warning. Or it is a circumstantial accusative by the known interpretation: i.e., making excuse or warning.

The majority read the dhal in both with a sukun.

Zayd ibn Thabit and his son Kharijah ibn Zayd, and Talhah, read them with a damma.

Al-Haramayn (Ibn Kathir and Nafi') and Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read them with a sukun in ('udhran) and a damma in (nudhuran).

The majority read ﴿'udhran aw nudhran﴾ with the conjunction "aw" (or).

Ibrahim al-Taymi and Qatadah read it with the conjunction "wa" (and), without an alif. The meaning is that the angels deliver the revelation as an excuse from Allah to His creation and as a warning of His punishment. Thus said al-Farra'. It was also said: an excuse for the righteous and a warning for the falsifiers.

Abu Ali al-Farisi said: it is possible that ('udhur) and (nudhur) with the heavy form are plurals of 'adhir and nadhir, as in His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [al-Najm: 56]. Then it would be accusative as a circumstantial element of the delivering: i.e., they deliver the reminder in the state of excuse and warning. Or they are two objects of (dhikran): i.e., remember excuse or warning.

Al-Mubarrad said: both in the heavy form are plurals, and the singular is 'adhir and nadhir.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the answer to the oath, saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised will surely occur﴾, i.e., what you are promised of the coming of the Hour and the Resurrection is certain to happen.

Then He, glorified is He, explained when that will occur, saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, i.e., their light is erased and their brightness departs. One says "tamasa al-shay'" when it is effaced and its trace disappears.

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾, i.e., it is opened and cleft. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the sky will be opened and will become gates﴾ [al-Naba': 19].

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, i.e., they are uprooted from their places swiftly. One says "nasafta al-shay'" and "ansaftuhu" when you take it swiftly.

Al-Kalbi said: they are leveled with the earth. The Arabs say: "The she-camel nasafat the pasture," when she grazes it. It was also said: they are made like grain which is winnowed with a winnowing shovel. Similar is His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be crumbled to dust﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 5]. The first view is preferable.

Al-Mubarrad said: nusifat means they are uprooted from their places.

﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾. The hamza in (uqqitat) is a substitution for a damma waw, and every waw that takes a damma where the damma is inherent may be replaced by a hamza. Abu 'Amr, Shaybah and al-A'raj read it with a waw, and the rest read it with a hamza. Al-waqt is the term at which a thing that is deferred to it occurs. The meaning: a time was set for them for the separation and judgment between them and their nations, as in His saying: ﴿On the day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. It was also said this refers to this world: i.e., the messengers were gathered for their appointed time which had been set for sending down punishment upon those who denied them. The first view is preferable. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: i.e., He made the Day of Judgment and the Separation a time for them. It was also said: they were sent at known times according to what Allah knows.

﴿For what day were they deferred?﴾ This interrogative is for magnification and wonder: i.e., for what great day, at which the servants marvel because of its severity and the abundance of its terrors, has a term been set for their gathering? The clause is a quoted saying of an implied verb, which is the answer to (idha), or it is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial element of the pronoun in (uqqitat). Al-Zajjaj said: the purpose of this appointing is to clarify the time at which they will attend to bear witness against their nations.

Then He explained this day, saying: ﴿For the Day of Separation﴾. Qatadah said: on it people will be separated by their deeds, to Paradise and to the Fire.

Then He magnified that day, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Separation is?﴾, i.e., what will inform you of the Day of Separation? He means it is a wondrous, awesome matter whose measure cannot be grasped. "Ma" is the subject and "adraka" its predicate, or the reverse, as Sibawayh preferred.

Then He mentioned the condition of those who denied that day, saying: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers!﴾, i.e., woe to them on that awesome day.
