**Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on Surah al-Mursalat (77), verses 29–50**

﴿Inṭalaqū ilā mā kuntum﴾ is governed by an implied verb of speech (*taqdir al-qawl*), meaning: it is said to them, as rebuke and reproach. ﴿Inṭalaqū ilā mā kuntum bihi tukadhdhibūn﴾ ("Go to that which you used to deny") in the world. The keepers of Hell (*khazanat Jahannam*) say this to them. That is: proceed to the punishment you used to deny, which is the punishment of the Fire. ﴿Inṭalaqū ilā ẓillin dhī thalāth shuʿab﴾ ("Go to a shade with three branches"): that is, to a shade of the smoke of Hell which has risen and then split into three columns, in which you will remain until the reckoning is finished. This is the nature of a great smoke: when it rises, it branches into divisions.

The majority of readers (*al-Jumhur*) read *inṭalaqū* in both places in the imperative form, for emphasis.

Ruways, on the authority of Yaʿqub, read the second occurrence in the past tense (*al-māḍī*): that is, when they were commanded to set out, they complied and set out.

It has also been said that the "shade" here means the *surādiq* (the enclosing tent), which is a tongue of fire that surrounds them. It then divides into three branches and shades them until the reckoning of them is finished; after that they go on to the Fire.

It has also been said that it is the shade of *yaḥmūm* (black smoke), as in His words: ﴿in scorching wind and boiling water and a shade of black smoke﴾, as has already been mentioned.

Then Allah, glorified is He, described this shade, mocking them, saying: ﴿Neither cool nor protective against the blaze﴾: that is, it gives no shade from the heat and does not protect against the flame.

Al-Kalbi said: it does not turn away the heat of Hell from you.

Then He described the Fire, saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a *qaṣr*﴾: that is, each spark it throws is as large as one of the great palaces (*quṣūr*). *Sharar* is what flies off from the fire scattered in pieces, and *qaṣr* is a great building.

It has also been said that *qaṣr* is the plural of *qaṣrah* (with a silent ṣād), like *ḥumr* and *ḥumrah*, or *tamr* and *tamrah*, and that it means a single piece of thick, heavy firewood.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are the large roots of trees. It has also been said that they are their necks (*aʿnāquhu*).

The majority read *ka-l-qaṣr* with a silent ṣād (*bi-iskān al-ṣād*), which is the singular of *quṣūr*, as already mentioned. Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Ḥumayd and al-Sulami read it with a vowelled ṣād (*bi-fatḥ al-ṣād*), meaning the necks of palm trees. The word *qaṣarah* means "neck", and its plural is *qaṣr* and *qaṣarāt*.

Qatadah said: the necks of camels.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr read it with a kasra on the qāf and a fatḥa on the ṣād, which is also a plural of *qaṣrah*, like *badr* and *badrah*, or *qaṣʿ* and *qaṣʿah*.

The majority read *bi-sharar* with a fatḥa on the shīn. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Miqsam read it with a kasra on the shīn and an alif between the two rāʾs. ʿIsa read it likewise, except with a fatḥa on the shīn. These are different dialects (*lughāt*).

Then He likened the sparks in respect of their colour, saying: ﴿As if they were yellow camels (*jimālatun ṣufr*)﴾. *Jimālah* is a plural of *jimāl*, which means camels, or a plural of *jammālah* (a rope-maker's cable).

The majority read *jimālāt* with a kasra on the jīm. Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾi and Ḥafṣ read *jimālah* as the plural of *jamal* (camel). Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and Abu Rajaʾ read *jumālāt* with a ḍamma on the jīm, meaning ship-ropes (*ḥibāl al-sufun*).

Al-Wahidi said: the word *ṣufr* means "black" in the view of the exegetes (*al-mufassirūn*).

Al-Farrāʾ said: *ṣufr* means the blackness of camels. No black camel is seen without a tinge of yellow in it, and for that reason the Arabs called black camels *ṣufr*.

It has been said that when sparks fly off and fall, and have something of the colour of fire in them, they most resemble black camels. From this is the saying of the poet:

*Those are my horses and those are my mounts; they are yellow, and their young are like raisins.*

That is, they are black.

It has been said that this view is impossible in the language, since a thing cannot have a small admixture of something else and then be entirely attributed to that admixture. How strange is the one who says this, when Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿jimālatun ṣufr﴾.

It has been answered that its meaning is this: the Fire was created from light, so it is bright. When Allah created Jahannam, which is the place of the Fire, He filled that place with that fire, and sent to it His authority and His wrath. It became black from His authority, grew blacker, and became blacker than anything else. Thus its sparks are black, because they come from black fire.

I say: this answer does not refute what the objector said, because his statement, in terms of what occurs in the Noble Book here, describes the Fire as yellow. If the matter were as the answerer stated, namely that the Fire and its sparks are black, Allah would have said: "as if they were black camels." However, since the Arabs call black things *aṣfar* (yellow), there is no problem left, for the Qur'an was revealed in their language, and trustworthy authorities have transmitted that usage from them. So what is in the Qur'an here follows this Arabic usage.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ of the messengers of Allah and His signs.

﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾: that is, they will not talk. Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said that the Day of Resurrection has stations (*mawāqif*); in some of them they speak, and in some of them a seal is placed on their mouths so that they do not speak. We have already mentioned this way of reconciling the verses in more than one place.

It has also been said that this refers to the time of their entry into the Fire, when they will not speak, because the stations of questioning and reckoning will have ended.

Al-Ḥasan said: they will not speak with any proof, even though they will be speaking.

The majority read *yawmun* with a ḍamma (*rafʿ*), as the predicate of the demonstrative (*ism al-ishārah*). Zayd ibn ʿAli, al-Aʿraj, al-Aʿmash, Abu Ḥayah, and ʿĀṣim in one transmission from him read it with a fatḥa, because it is built (*bināʾ*) on the fatḥa due to its being attached to a verb. Its position is in the nominative as predicate. It has also been said that it is in the accusative as an adverb of time (*ẓarf*). The demonstrative *hādhā* refers to the threat mentioned earlier, as if it were said: this punishment mentioned is due on the day when they will not speak.

﴿Nor will they be permitted to offer excuses﴾. The majority read *yu’dhanu* in the passive voice. Zayd ibn ʿAli read *lā yaʾdhanu* in the active voice, meaning: Allah will not permit them, that is, they will have no permission from Allah, so they will have no excuse, without making the excuse a consequence of permission, as would be the case if the verb were in the subjunctive (*naṣb*).

Al-Farrāʾ said: the *fāʾ* in *fa-yaʿtadhirūn* is coordinated with *yu’dhanu*. This is permitted because the endings of the discourse are in *nūn*. If he had said *fa-yaʿtadhirū* it would not have matched the verse-endings. He has also said: ﴿It will not be decreed upon them so that they die﴾ [Fāṭir 35:36], with the subjunctive, and both are correct.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, for what the messengers called them to and warned them of its consequence.

﴿This is the Day of Decision; We have gathered you and the former peoples﴾: that is, it is said to them: this is the Day of Decision, on which judgment is passed among creatures and truth is distinguished from falsehood. The address in *jamaʿnākum* is to the disbelievers of the time of our Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ), and by "the former ones" is meant the disbelievers of earlier nations.

﴿So if you have a scheme﴾: that is, if you are able to devise a scheme now, then devise it against Me. This is rebuke and reproach for them.

Muqatil said: he means, if you have a stratagem, then employ it for yourselves. It has also been said that the meaning is: if you are able to wage war, then wage it. It has also been said that this is the speech of the Prophet (ﷺ), and so it is like the words of Hud: ﴿So plot against me all together, and give me no respite﴾ [Hud 11:55].

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, because their helplessness and the falsity of what they held in the world became manifest to them.

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the believers, saying: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in shades and springs﴾: that is, in the shade of trees and the shade of palaces, unlike the shade of the disbelievers, which is of smoke or of fire, as has already been mentioned.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: by "the God-fearing" is meant those who guard against associating partners with Allah, because the whole surah, from beginning to end, is a rebuke of the disbelievers for their disbelief.

Al-Razi said: this verse must be mentioned for this purpose, otherwise the surah would fall apart in its composition and order. The composition is only complete if the promise to the believers is made because of their faith; but making it a cause of obedience does not fit the composition. So he said. By "springs" are meant rivers, and by "fruits" what they take delight in, from what their souls desire and their appetites call for.

﴿Eat and drink with ease for what you used to do﴾: that is, it is said to them. The clause is implicitly introduced by *qawl*, and it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state (*ḥāl*) of the God-fearing. The *bāʾ* is causal (*sababiyyah*): that is, because of what you used to do in the world of good deeds.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers﴾: that is, by a reward like this great one, We reward the good-doers for their deeds. The majority read *fī ẓilāl* (in shades). Al-Aʿmash, al-Zuhri, Ṭalḥah and al-Aʿraj read *fī ẓulul*, the plural of *ẓullah*.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, since they are in great misery, while the believers are in lasting bliss.

﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed you are criminals﴾: the clause is implicitly introduced by *qawl* and is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state of the deniers. That is: woe is established for them at the time when this is said to them, as a reminder of their state in the world. Or it is said to them this in the world. The *mujrimūn* are those who associate partners with Allah. Although this is in form an imperative, in meaning it is a threat and a severe warning.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾: He repeated it to increase the rebuke and reproach.

﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾: that is, when they are commanded to pray, they do not pray.

Muqatil said: this was revealed concerning the tribe of Thaqīf, who refused to pray after the Prophet (ﷺ) had commanded them to. They said: "We will not bow, for it is a disgrace upon us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no good in a religion that has no bowing or prostration in it."

It has also been said that this is said to them only in the Hereafter, when they are called to prostrate and cannot.

It has also been said that by bowing is meant obedience and humility.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ of the commands and prohibitions of Allah, glorified is He.

﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾: that is, in what statement after the Qur'an will they believe, if they do not believe in it?

He said: I heard him being asked about His words: ﴿yellow camels﴾, and he said: they are ship-ropes, joined one to another until they are like men's waists.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, because their helplessness and the falsity of what they held in the world became manifest to them.

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the believers, saying: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in shades and springs﴾: that is, in the shade of trees and the shade of palaces, unlike the shade of the disbelievers, which is of smoke or of fire, as has already been mentioned.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: by "the God-fearing" is meant those who guard against associating partners with Allah, because the whole surah, from beginning to end, is a rebuke of the disbelievers for their disbelief.

Al-Razi said: this verse must be mentioned for this purpose, otherwise the surah would fall apart in its composition and order. The composition is only complete if the promise to the believers is made because of their faith; but making it a cause of obedience does not fit the composition. So he said. By "springs" are meant rivers, and by "fruits" what they take delight in, from what their souls desire and their appetites call for.

﴿Eat and drink with ease for what you used to do﴾: that is, it is said to them. The clause is implicitly introduced by *qawl*, and it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state (*ḥāl*) of the God-fearing. The *bāʾ* is causal (*sababiyyah*): that is, because of what you used to do in the world of good deeds.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers﴾: that is, by a reward like this great one, We reward the good-doers for their deeds. The majority read *fī ẓilāl* (in shades). Al-Aʿmash, al-Zuhri, Ṭalḥah and al-Aʿraj read *fī ẓulul*, the plural of *ẓullah*.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, since they are in great misery, while the believers are in lasting bliss.

﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed you are criminals﴾: the clause is implicitly introduced by *qawl* and is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state of the deniers. That is: woe is established for them at the time when this is said to them, as a reminder of their state in the world. Or it is said to them this in the world. The *mujrimūn* are those who associate partners with Allah. Although this is in form an imperative, in meaning it is a threat and a severe warning.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾: He repeated it to increase the rebuke and reproach.

﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾: that is, when they are commanded to pray, they do not pray.

Muqatil said: this was revealed concerning the tribe of Thaqīf, who refused to pray after the Prophet (ﷺ) had commanded them to. They said: "We will not bow, for it is a disgrace upon us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no good in a religion that has no bowing or prostration in it."

It has also been said that this is said to them only in the Hereafter, when they are called to prostrate and cannot.

It has also been said that by bowing is meant obedience and humility.

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ of the commands and prohibitions of Allah, glorified is He.

﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾: that is, in what statement after the Qur'an will they believe, if they do not believe in it?

The majority read *yu'minūn* with the *yāʾ* (third person, *ghaybah*). Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission from him, and Yaʿqub, read it with the *tāʾ* (second person, *khiṭāb*).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Ḥatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿like a qaṣr with sparks﴾, that he said: like a great palace. And concerning His words ﴿yellow camels﴾, he said: pieces of copper.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Hannad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ḥakim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted by way of ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn ʿAbis, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas being asked about His words: ﴿Indeed it throws sparks like a qaṣr﴾, and he said: We used to take a piece of wood of three cubits or less, and we would raise it for the winter, and we called it the *qaṣr*.

He said: I heard him being asked about His words: ﴿yellow camels﴾, and he said: they are ship-ropes, joined one to another until they are like men's waists.

The wording of al-Bukhari is: We used to take a piece of wood three cubits long or more and raise it for the winter, and we called it the *qaṣr*. ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾: ship-ropes, joined together until they are like men's waists.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him that he read *ka-l-qaṣar* with a fatḥa on the qāf and the ṣād. He said: *qaṣar al-nakhl*, meaning the necks.

Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted from him that he said: the Arabs in the Jāhiliyyah used to say, "Cut us wood (*aqṣirū lanā al-ḥaṭab*)," and it would be cut to the size of a cubit or two cubits.

Saʿid ibn Manṣur, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Ḥatim and al-Ṭabarani in *al-Awsaṭ* transmitted from Ibn Masʿud, concerning His words: ﴿It throws sparks like a qaṣr﴾, that he said: it is not like trees and mountains, but like cities and fortresses.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words "like a qaṣr", that he said: it is the palace (*al-qaṣr*). And concerning His words "yellow camels", he said: the camels.

al-Ḥakim, and he authenticated it, transmitted by way of ʿIkrimah, who said: Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn ʿAbbas about His words: ﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾, ﴿Then not a sound will you hear except a whisper﴾, ﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾, and ﴿Here, read my record!﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah 69:19]. Ibn ʿAbbas said to him: Woe to you! Have you asked about this of anyone before me? He said: No. He said: If you had asked, you would have been destroyed. Did not Allah say: ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Ḥajj 22:47]? He said: Yes. He said: Then for each measure of a day of these days there is a colour of colours.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾, that he said: they will be called on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate and will be unable to, because in the world they did not prostrate to Allah.
